## Environmental compliance inspector — federal variant (P1)

*Function:* Establish, with defensible evidence, whether regulated facilities and sites meet their permits and rules, and start the response the enforcement policy requires.

*X4 match:* `skos:broadMatch` (confidence 0.6, applies to: all; candidate agent draft, evidence J). *Authority position (editorial):* regulator.

### Developmental and full performance — indicative band GS-5 to GS-7 (entry); GS-9 to GS-11 (journey) (not a classification criterion)

**Major duties (agent draft, in record order)**

*% time: set by the supervisor; EMST supplies none before job analysis.*

*Critical and needed-at-entry tasks: Assessment pending (job analysis).*

- **Conduct regulatory compliance inspections**
  - Plan a compliance inspection from the facility's permit, compliance history and monitoring reports, listing the conditions to verify and the evidence to collect
  - Inspect a permitted facility or site against its permit conditions and applicable rules, recording observations, measurements and samples as evidence *(formation task, editorial draft)*
  - Collect samples and photographs during an inspection under chain-of-custody procedures, so that the evidence is admissible in an enforcement proceeding
  - Write an inspection report stating findings of fact for each condition inspected, separating the inspector's observations from conclusions
- **Measure water quality and survey aquatic communities in the field**
  - Collect grab water samples at locations and depths that represent the condition of interest, recording flow and site conditions at collection *(formation task, editorial draft)*
- **Manage field sample custody and field quality control**
  - Complete chain-of-custody records for every sample from collection to laboratory receipt, recording each transfer, seal and temperature check
  - Collect field duplicates, splits and blanks at the frequency the sampling plan specifies, labelling them so the laboratory cannot identify them
- **Develop and resolve environmental enforcement cases**
  - Investigate a reported environmental violation, establishing the facts, responsible party and applicable requirement before recommending an enforcement response
  - Assemble the evidence file for an enforcement case, linking each alleged violation to the inspection findings, records and samples that prove it
- **Target inspections and verify compliance using monitoring data and analytics**
  - Review automated anomaly flags in facility monitoring reports, confirming or dismissing each flag against the underlying data before referral
  - Verify a facility's self-reported emissions or discharge values against independent remote-sensing or ambient data, stating the discrepancy and its uncertainty
- **Assure the quality of environmental data from collection to release**
  - Audit an environmental dataset on a set schedule, identifying errors and anomalies and recording each correction with its basis. *(formation task, editorial draft)*
- **Validate AI-generated work products before professional use**
  - Check an AI-assisted regulatory analysis or compliance summary against the applicable legal text and source records before it enters a decision document. *(formation task, editorial draft)*
  - Verify an AI-generated field product, such as a condition map or drafted inspection note, against observations made at the site before it is relied on *(formation task, editorial draft)*
- **Provide compliance and technical assistance to regulated entities and local governments**
  - Visit a small regulated facility on request to identify compliance gaps, recommending corrective steps without initiating enforcement where policy allows
  - Answer compliance questions from regulated entities through a help line or portal, recording each question and the guidance given for consistency review
- **Work safely on hazardous, industrial and energized field sites**
  - Identify signs of potential hazardous materials at a field site, such as drums, stained soil, odours or unusual debris, before disturbing them
  - Follow a site health and safety plan at a contaminated or industrial site, observing zone boundaries, air-monitoring action levels and decontamination steps
  - Keep required clearances from energized lines, confined spaces and operating machinery during field work at utility and industrial sites, stopping when clearance cannot be held
- **Apply safety practices and stop-work authority across field, facility and incident settings**
  - Exercise stop-work authority when field, facility or incident conditions exceed the stated safety limits of the assignment
- **Maintain independence and manage conflicts of interest across the regulator-regulated boundary**
  - Recuse from a decision or review in which a former employer or client has an interest, documenting the recusal and the reassignment of the work
  - Disclose financial, employment or relationship interests that could affect an assignment before work begins, using the organization's conflict form
- **Build and maintain a defensible administrative record**
  - Index documents into the administrative record with dates, authors and provenance labels, marking which content was produced with AI assistance

**Factor 1 — knowledge required (draft language; target levels are editorial drafts)**

- Knowledge of and skill in: conduct regulatory compliance inspections (EMST target entry L1, journey L2, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: develop and resolve environmental enforcement cases (EMST target journey L2, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: target inspections and verify compliance using monitoring data and analytics (EMST target journey L2, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: manage field sample custody and field quality control (EMST target entry L1, journey L2, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: build and maintain a defensible administrative record (EMST target entry L1, journey L2, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: work safely on hazardous, industrial and energized field sites (EMST target entry L1, journey L2, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: maintain independence and manage conflicts of interest across the regulator-regulated boundary (EMST target entry L1, journey L2, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: apply safety practices and stop-work authority across field, facility and incident settings (EMST target entry L1, journey L2, editorial draft).
  - Stop-work authority lets any worker halt a task they judge unsafe; the task resumes only after the hazard is assessed and the plan revised, and the person who stopped it is not penalized.
  - A no-blame incident review separates system and condition causes from individual error and sanctions only reckless or wilful acts, so that people keep reporting near misses.
- Knowledge of and skill in: validate AI-generated work products before professional use (EMST target entry L1, journey L2, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: provide compliance and technical assistance to regulated entities and local governments (EMST target entry L1, journey L2, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: record field observations with protocol fidelity and data integrity (EMST target entry L1, journey L2, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: assure the quality of environmental data from collection to release (EMST target entry L1, journey L2, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: maintain the integrity of regulatory and scientific findings under institutional pressure (EMST target entry L1, journey L2, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: communicate environmental and health risks under uncertainty (EMST target entry L1, journey L2, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: measure water quality and survey aquatic communities in the field (EMST target entry L1, journey L1, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: interpret and question environmental data products in everyday work (EMST target entry L1, journey L1, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: use AI tools responsibly in everyday environmental work (EMST target entry L1, journey L1, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: record provenance and AI involvement in work products (EMST target entry L1, journey L1, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: communicate technical environmental information in writing and speech (EMST target entry L1, journey L2, editorial draft).

## Environmental review specialist — federal variant (P1)

*Function:* Establish, document and defend what a proposed action's effects are and which review it requires, so that the deciding official acts on a defensible record.

*X4 match:* `skos:broadMatch` (confidence 0.6, applies to: all; candidate agent draft, evidence J). *Authority position (editorial):* resource-manager.

### Developmental and full performance — indicative band GS-9 to GS-11 (journey) (not a classification criterion)

**Major duties (agent draft, in record order)**

*% time: set by the supervisor; EMST supplies none before job analysis.*

*Critical and needed-at-entry tasks: Assessment pending (job analysis).*

- **Conduct environmental impact review of proposed actions**
  - Prepare an environmental assessment of a proposed action, analyzing the reasonably foreseeable effects of the action and its alternatives within the procedure's page and time limits *(formation task, editorial draft)*
  - Scope the review of a proposed action with cooperating agencies and the public, setting the purpose, alternatives and effects boundaries the analysis will cover *(formation task, editorial draft)*
  - Verify AI-drafted sections of an environmental document against the project record, correcting unsupported statements and recording which text was machine-drafted
- **Select, justify and document the appropriate level of environmental review**
  - Determine whether a proposed action requires an environmental assessment or a full impact statement, documenting the significance reasoning in the project record
  - Screen a proposed action against the agency's exclusion categories and extraordinary-circumstance criteria, recording the screening result and its basis for the official
  - Review automated exclusion-screening results for a batch of routine actions, confirming or overriding each flagged extraordinary circumstance
- **Coordinate lead, cooperating and participating agencies to a shared schedule**
  - Coordinate review steps with other agencies holding authority over the same action, so that duplicated analyses and conflicting requirements are identified early
  - Update public milestone and dashboard entries for a covered project, reconciling each entry against agency source documents every reporting period
- **Build and maintain a defensible administrative record**
  - Index documents into the administrative record with dates, authors and provenance labels, marking which content was produced with AI assistance
  - Confirm that every substantive comment in a docket has a reasoned response, sampling machine-grouped comments for unique points the grouping missed
- **Analyze regulatory, planning and public-comment text at scale with traceable citations**
  - Code a public comment set into themes with machine assistance, tracing every coded statement to its source passage before summarizing for decision-makers. *(formation task, editorial draft)*
  - Extract requirements from a plan or permit into a table with machine assistance, verifying each row against the cited page and paragraph.
- **Validate AI-generated work products before professional use**
  - Sample machine-grouped public comments to confirm that substantive and unique comments were not merged away before responses are drafted.
- **Review effects of proposed actions on historic properties and resolve them through consultation**
  - Define the area of potential effects for a proposed undertaking, documenting the direct and indirect effect pathways that justify its boundary
  - Assess whether a proposed action would adversely affect each eligible property, recording the criteria and evidence applied to each finding
- **Assess effects on protected species and conduct interagency consultation on proposed actions**
  - Prepare a biological assessment for a proposed action, stating the effects determination for each listed species and critical habitat with supporting evidence
  - Review an effects determination drafted with AI assistance against the species and project records, correcting each conclusion the records do not support
  - Compile species and habitat occurrence information for an action area, documenting the sources and survey dates used for each listed species
- **Analyze cumulative burdens and distributional effects of environmental decisions**
  - Screen a proposed project's area for existing environmental and health burdens using screening indicators, recording each indicator's source, date and known limitations
- **Design proportionate public engagement when participation is discretionary**
  - Write an engagement plan stating who will be engaged, by which methods and when, and why that scope fits the decision

**Factor 1 — knowledge required (draft language; target levels are editorial drafts)**

- Knowledge of and skill in: conduct environmental impact review of proposed actions (EMST target journey L2, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: select, justify and document the appropriate level of environmental review (EMST target journey L2, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: build and maintain a defensible administrative record (EMST target journey L2, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: direct and evaluate applicant- or contractor-prepared environmental documents (EMST target journey L2, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: coordinate lead, cooperating and participating agencies to a shared schedule (EMST target journey L2, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: assess effects on protected species and conduct interagency consultation on proposed actions (EMST target journey L2, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: review effects of proposed actions on historic properties and resolve them through consultation (EMST target journey L2, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: analyze regulatory, planning and public-comment text at scale with traceable citations (EMST target journey L2, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: validate AI-generated work products before professional use (EMST target journey L2, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: analyze cumulative burdens and distributional effects of environmental decisions (EMST target journey L2, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: design proportionate public engagement when participation is discretionary (EMST target journey L2, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: identify and analyze the parties affected by or interested in a decision (EMST target journey L2, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: quantify and communicate uncertainty for environmental decisions (EMST target journey L2, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: communicate environmental and health risks under uncertainty (EMST target journey L2, editorial draft).

## Air quality specialist — federal variant (P2)

*Function:* Bring and keep air quality within standards through monitoring, planning, permitting and inspection.

*X4 match:* `skos:broadMatch` (confidence 0.55, applies to: all; candidate agent draft, evidence J). *Authority position (editorial):* regulator.

### Developmental and full performance — indicative band GS-9 to GS-11 (journey) (not a classification criterion)

**Major duties (agent draft, in record order)**

*% time: set by the supervisor; EMST supplies none before job analysis.*

*Critical and needed-at-entry tasks: Assessment pending (job analysis).*

- **Build emissions inventories and air quality models for attainment planning**
  - Compile a point, area, mobile and natural source emissions inventory for a planning year with documented methods and activity data
  - Run a photochemical model for an attainment demonstration under an approved modelling protocol, documenting model performance against monitored data
  - Review a permit applicant's dispersion modelling analysis against the agreed protocol and guidance before accepting its conclusions
  - Check emissions estimates generated automatically from activity or sensor data against source tests and inventory methods before inclusion
- **Issue environmental permits and resource-use authorizations as the deciding authority**
  - Determine whether a proposed modification at a stationary source triggers major new source review from emissions increases and netting
  - Draft operating permit conditions for a major stationary air source with monitoring sufficient to show compliance with each applicable requirement
  - Review a control technology determination submitted with an air permit application against comparable sources and cost criteria
  - Check permit conditions drafted from a template or AI tool against the source's applicable requirements before public notice
- **Operate ambient air monitoring networks to regulatory quality-assurance criteria**
  - Audit a regulatory air monitor's flow and gas calibration against transfer standards following the quality assurance project plan
  - Validate a quarter's ambient monitoring data against quality-assurance criteria, flagging or invalidating values before data certification
  - Collocate low-cost sensors with a regulatory monitor to derive correction factors, documenting sensor performance before the data are published
- **Conduct regulatory compliance inspections**
  - Inspect a permitted facility or site against its permit conditions and applicable rules, recording observations, measurements and samples as evidence *(formation task, editorial draft)*

## Environmental permit writer — federal variant (P1)

*Function:* Turn an application and the governing standards into permit conditions that are measurable, enforceable and traceable to their legal and technical basis.

*X4 match:* `skos:broadMatch` (confidence 0.55, applies to: all; candidate agent draft, evidence J). *Authority position (editorial):* regulator.

### Developmental and full performance — indicative band GS-9 to GS-11 (journey) (not a classification criterion)

**Major duties (agent draft, in record order)**

*% time: set by the supervisor; EMST supplies none before job analysis.*

*Critical and needed-at-entry tasks: Assessment pending (job analysis).*

- **Issue environmental permits and resource-use authorizations as the deciding authority**
  - Review a permit application for administrative and technical completeness, issuing a deficiency notice that lists each missing element and its basis
  - Derive permit limits and conditions from the applicable technical standards and the facility's technical record, documenting the calculation basis for each limit
  - Draft a permit and its fact sheet so that each condition is measurable, enforceable and traceable to its legal or technical basis *(formation task, editorial draft)*
  - Review an AI-drafted permit or fact sheet against the application record and permit template, correcting each condition that lacks a traceable basis *(formation task, editorial draft)*
- **Draft enforceable, implementable binding instruments**
  - Write policy or instrument language that states each obligation, obligated party, deadline and verification method so that compliance can be determined
  - Test draft permit conditions or agreement terms against compliance-verification and legal-challenge scenarios, recording each term revised and why
  - Verify each term of an AI-generated first draft of an instrument against the governing authority and record before the draft enters review
- **Map the decision authority and procedural pathway for a proposed action**
  - Review a project proposal to identify every authorization, consultation and review it triggers, recording the governing procedure version for each
- **Process permit applications and administer issued authorizations**
  - Review automated eligibility and completeness checks on electronic permit applications, correcting misclassified applications before decisions are issued
  - Maintain permit records and electronic case files, tracking holders' reporting and expiry dates and referring missed conditions for follow-up
  - Explain permit conditions and environmental responsibilities to permit holders before use begins, recording each holder's acknowledgment of the conditions
- **Track regulatory change and translate it into operating guidance**
  - Screen automated regulatory-change alerts for a program each week, confirming which items affect its decisions and recording why the rest do not
- **Build and maintain a defensible administrative record**
  - Index documents into the administrative record with dates, authors and provenance labels, marking which content was produced with AI assistance
- **Provide compliance and technical assistance to regulated entities and local governments**
  - Answer compliance questions from regulated entities through a help line or portal, recording each question and the guidance given for consistency review
- **Maintain independence and manage conflicts of interest across the regulator-regulated boundary**
  - Recuse from a decision or review in which a former employer or client has an interest, documenting the recusal and the reassignment of the work
- **Validate AI-generated work products before professional use**
  - Check an AI-assisted regulatory analysis or compliance summary against the applicable legal text and source records before it enters a decision document. *(formation task, editorial draft)*

## Enforcement case manager — federal variant (P2)

*Function:* Bring regulated parties back into compliance through defensible, proportionate enforcement actions.

*X4 match:* `skos:broadMatch` (confidence 0.55, applies to: all; candidate agent draft, evidence J). *Authority position (editorial):* regulator.

### Developmental and full performance — indicative band GS-9 to GS-11 (journey) (not a classification criterion)

**Major duties (agent draft, in record order)**

*% time: set by the supervisor; EMST supplies none before job analysis.*

- **Develop and resolve environmental enforcement cases**
  - Investigate a reported environmental violation, establishing the facts, responsible party and applicable requirement before recommending an enforcement response
  - Assemble the evidence file for an enforcement case, linking each alleged violation to the inspection findings, records and samples that prove it
  - Calculate a proposed civil penalty under the program's penalty policy, documenting the gravity, economic benefit and adjustment factors applied
- **Build and maintain a defensible administrative record**
  - Publish comment summaries and the agency's responses in the record, linking each response to the substantive comments it answers
  - Index documents into the administrative record with dates, authors and provenance labels, marking which content was produced with AI assistance
  - Write the reasoned explanation that links the evidence in the record to each choice made in a decision
- **Assess litigation exposure and design decisions for resilience on remand**
  - Identify the claims a proposed decision is likely to face, rating each claim's likelihood under current deference, standing and remedy doctrine
  - Review a decision record with counsel before issuance, listing the record gaps that weaken the reasoned explanation and the fix for each
- **Negotiate permit conditions, mitigation and agreements using interest-based methods**
  - Convert a negotiated agreement into implementable terms, checking each term against a verification method before signature
  - Prepare a negotiation brief stating own and counterpart interests, alternatives to agreement, the issue list and the limits of one's authority

  - Inspect a permitted facility or site against its permit conditions and applicable rules, recording observations, measurements and samples as evidence *(formation task, editorial draft)*
  - Collect samples and photographs during an inspection under chain-of-custody procedures, so that the evidence is admissible in an enforcement proceeding
  - Select the response the enforcement policy sets for each inspection finding, issuing a notice of violation, assistance letter or referral
- **Target inspections and verify compliance using monitoring data and analytics**
  - Rank regulated facilities for inspection using compliance history and monitoring data, documenting the risk factors and weights in the targeting method
  - Review automated anomaly flags in facility monitoring reports, confirming or dismissing each flag against the underlying data before referral
- **Maintain the integrity of regulatory and scientific findings under institutional pressure**
  - Document any instruction or pressure to alter a regulatory or scientific finding, recording who made it, what was requested and the response given
  - Disclose conflicts of interest, uncertainty, dissenting views and AI assistance in a regulatory submission or public document, following the organization's integrity policy
  - Write quality-assurance and escalation procedures that protect the independence of regulatory findings, including peer-review steps and documentation of changes
- **Draft enforceable, implementable binding instruments**
  - Write policy or instrument language that states each obligation, obligated party, deadline and verification method so that compliance can be determined
  - Review a proposed policy or instrument for consistency with governing law, existing instruments and agency authority, listing each conflict found
- **Maintain independence and manage conflicts of interest across the regulator-regulated boundary**
  - Apply post-employment restrictions when moving between a regulator and a regulated party, obtaining written ethics advice before contact on covered matters
  - Disclose financial, employment or relationship interests that could affect an assignment before work begins, using the organization's conflict form
- **Resolve conflicts and mediate disputes over environmental decisions**
  - Restate each party's concern during a tense exchange until the party confirms it was understood, so that the exchange can continue

## Drinking water programme analyst — federal variant (P2)

*Function:* Assure that public water systems deliver water meeting drinking water requirements, and act when they do not.

*X4 match:* `skos:broadMatch` (confidence 0.55, applies to: all; candidate agent draft, evidence J). *Authority position (editorial):* regulator.

### Developmental and full performance — indicative band GS-9 to GS-11 (journey) (not a classification criterion)

**Major duties (agent draft, in record order)**

*% time: set by the supervisor; EMST supplies none before job analysis.*

*Critical and needed-at-entry tasks: Assessment pending (job analysis).*

- **Assure public water system compliance with drinking water requirements**
  - Determine the monitoring schedule, contaminant limits and treatment-technique requirements that apply to a public water system from its source, size and treatment
  - Conduct a sanitary survey of a public water system's source, treatment, storage, distribution and operations, documenting significant deficiencies
  - Review a utility's service-line inventory and lead sampling plan against applicable requirements and return deficiencies for correction
  - Issue a violation notice with a public-notification directive when monitoring results exceed a contaminant limit or required monitoring is missed
- **Operate within, or oversee, delegated and assumed regulatory programs**
  - Respond to an overseeing agency's objection to a permit issued under delegated authority, revising the permit or defending it with a written record
  - Assess whether a proposed change to program rules keeps them at least as stringent as the delegated authority requires, documenting each provision compared
- **Conduct regulatory compliance inspections**
  - Inspect a permitted facility or site against its permit conditions and applicable rules, recording observations, measurements and samples as evidence *(formation task, editorial draft)*
  - Collect samples and photographs during an inspection under chain-of-custody procedures, so that the evidence is admissible in an enforcement proceeding
- **Provide compliance and technical assistance to regulated entities and local governments**
  - Answer compliance questions from regulated entities through a help line or portal, recording each question and the guidance given for consistency review
  - Visit a small regulated facility on request to identify compliance gaps, recommending corrective steps without initiating enforcement where policy allows
  - Deliver compliance training to local government staff responsible for a delegated or shared program, testing participants on the obligations covered
- **Track regulatory change and translate it into operating guidance**
  - Screen automated regulatory-change alerts for a program each week, confirming which items affect its decisions and recording why the rest do not
  - Update program procedures and templates to a new governing version, recording which pending actions follow the old and new versions
- **Communicate environmental and health risks under uncertainty**
  - Answer public questions about an uncertain environmental risk at a meeting or by phone using the current message map
  - Draft a public advisory that states the hazard, the people affected, the uncertainty and the protective action in plain language
  - Prepare a shared message map with partner agencies for an emerging environmental or health incident
- **Administer environmental financial assistance to local governments**
  - Close out a financial assistance award, reconciling final costs, outcomes and compliance records against the award terms
  - Monitor funded projects' disbursements and milestones, withholding payment where required documentation or performance is missing
- **Build and maintain a defensible administrative record**
  - Publish comment summaries and the agency's responses in the record, linking each response to the substantive comments it answers
- **Investigate and manage emerging contaminants across media**
  - Interpret emerging-contaminant results against current and proposed criteria, stating how the conclusions change if the criteria change.
- **Collect trace-level and genetic environmental samples without contamination**
  - Collect a first-draw lead and copper sample at a sampling-pool residence following the stagnation and container protocol, documenting any deviation

## Facility environmental compliance specialist — federal variant (P4)

*Function:* Keep a regulated facility in documented compliance with its permits, rules and reporting obligations.

*X4 match:* `skos:broadMatch` (confidence 0.5, applies to: federal installations; candidate agent draft, evidence J). *Authority position (editorial):* regulated-party.

### Developmental and full performance — indicative band GS-5 to GS-7 (entry); GS-9 to GS-11 (journey) (not a classification criterion)

**Major duties (agent draft, in record order)**

*% time: set by the supervisor; EMST supplies none before job analysis.*

*Critical and needed-at-entry tasks: Assessment pending (job analysis).*

- **Manage a regulated facility's environmental compliance system and obligations calendar**
  - Develop a facility compliance checklist and procedures from its permits and applicable rules, assigning an owner and deadline to each obligation
  - Update the facility compliance calendar when a permit, rule or reporting requirement changes, notifying each obligation owner of the change
  - Prepare a periodic compliance report for the facility, checking reported values against source data before the responsible official certifies it
  - Investigate a permit exceedance at the facility, identifying the root cause and documenting corrective actions and the notice given to the agency
- **Manage regulated-entity disclosure and compliance across divergent regimes**
  - Prepare a mandatory disclosure report from controlled data collected across operations, tracing each reported figure to its source system
- **Track regulatory change and translate it into operating guidance**
  - Screen automated regulatory-change alerts for a program each week, confirming which items affect its decisions and recording why the rest do not
  - Update program procedures and templates to a new governing version, recording which pending actions follow the old and new versions
- **Manage field sample custody and field quality control**
  - Complete chain-of-custody records for every sample from collection to laboratory receipt, recording each transfer, seal and temperature check
  - Collect field duplicates, splits and blanks at the frequency the sampling plan specifies, labelling them so the laboratory cannot identify them
- **Work safely on hazardous, industrial and energized field sites**
  - Follow a site health and safety plan at a contaminated or industrial site, observing zone boundaries, air-monitoring action levels and decontamination steps
  - Identify signs of potential hazardous materials at a field site, such as drums, stained soil, odours or unusual debris, before disturbing them
- **Apply safety practices and stop-work authority across field, facility and incident settings**
  - Exercise stop-work authority when field, facility or incident conditions exceed the stated safety limits of the assignment
  - Deliver a pre-work safety briefing that covers site hazards, controls, communications and the stop-work procedure for the assigned work area
- **Maintain independence and manage conflicts of interest across the regulator-regulated boundary**
  - Apply post-employment restrictions when moving between a regulator and a regulated party, obtaining written ethics advice before contact on covered matters
  - Disclose financial, employment or relationship interests that could affect an assignment before work begins, using the organization's conflict form
- **Build and maintain a defensible administrative record**
  - Index documents into the administrative record with dates, authors and provenance labels, marking which content was produced with AI assistance
- **Build organizational and jurisdictional greenhouse gas inventories for disclosure and reporting**
  - Compile a greenhouse gas inventory for an organization or jurisdiction, documenting boundaries, activity data, emission factors and methods for each source.
- **Map the decision authority and procedural pathway for a proposed action**
  - Track the status of each authorization for a project against the pathway plan, notifying the project team when a delay moves the critical path
- **Record provenance and AI involvement in work products**
  - Record the source, date, version, method and any AI tool used for a dataset or analysis, using the organization's provenance template.

  - Stop-work authority lets any worker halt a task they judge unsafe; the task resumes only after the hazard is assessed and the plan revised, and the person who stopped it is not penalized.
  - A no-blame incident review separates system and condition causes from individual error and sanctions only reckless or wilful acts, so that people keep reporting near misses.

## Remediation project manager — federal variant (P2)

*Function:* Bring contaminated sites to protective, documented end states through characterization, remedy selection and oversight.

*X4 match:* `skos:broadMatch` (confidence 0.5, applies to: all; candidate agent draft, evidence J). *Authority position (editorial):* regulator.

*Credential gates (issuer verified):* 1 not shown until the issuer is verified

### Developmental and full performance — indicative band GS-9 to GS-11 (journey) (not a classification criterion)

**Major duties (agent draft, in record order)**

*% time: set by the supervisor; EMST supplies none before job analysis.*

*Critical and needed-at-entry tasks: Assessment pending (job analysis).*

- **Select remedies for contaminated sites and oversee cleanup through long-term stewardship**
  - Oversee a remediation contractor's field work against the approved design and health and safety plan, documenting deviations and corrective actions
  - Decide from performance monitoring data whether to optimize, continue or transition an operating remedy, recording the evidence for the decision
  - Conduct a periodic review of a closed site's remedy and institutional controls, recording whether the remedy remains protective
- **Conduct environmental site assessment and site characterization**
  - Log soil cores and choose sample intervals in the field from lithology, staining, odor and field-screening readings
  - Oversee monitoring well installation and development, verifying screen placement against field lithology before the well is completed
  - Update the conceptual site model with new data, identifying the data gaps that still prevent a remedy decision
- **Assess human health risks from environmental exposures**
  - Conduct an exposure assessment for an environmental contaminant, identifying pathways, receptors and exposure concentrations with documented assumptions.
  - Calculate health risks from environmental exposures with the methods the applicable requirements specify, stating the uncertainty of each estimate.
  - Communicate health risk findings to affected communities and decision-makers, explaining what the estimates mean for exposure and action.
- **Manage field sample custody and field quality control**
  - Complete chain-of-custody records for every sample from collection to laboratory receipt, recording each transfer, seal and temperature check
  - Collect field duplicates, splits and blanks at the frequency the sampling plan specifies, labelling them so the laboratory cannot identify them
- **Deliver environmental projects to budget, schedule and quality**
  - Prepare progress reports for leadership from the project's tracking records, stating schedule and budget variance.
  - Break a large project into phased work packages with deliverables, dependencies and decision points
  - Maintain the project schedule baseline and record actual progress against it at each reporting period
- **Direct and evaluate applicant- or contractor-prepared environmental documents**
  - Document the agency's independent evaluation of a sponsor-prepared document before adoption, recording what was verified and what was changed
  - Issue scope and content standards to a sponsor's contractor preparing an environmental document, specifying data, methods and the agency's review checkpoints
- **Determine hazardous waste status and manage generator compliance**
  - Determine whether a waste stream is hazardous from process knowledge and laboratory data, documenting the listing and characteristic evaluation
  - Inspect satellite and central accumulation areas for container condition, labelling, dating and segregation, correcting deficiencies before shipment
- **Investigate and manage emerging contaminants across media**
  - Interpret emerging-contaminant results against current and proposed criteria, stating how the conclusions change if the criteria change.
- **Develop and resolve environmental enforcement cases**
  - Investigate a reported environmental violation, establishing the facts, responsible party and applicable requirement before recommending an enforcement response
  - Assemble the evidence file for an enforcement case, linking each alleged violation to the inspection findings, records and samples that prove it
- **Communicate environmental and health risks under uncertainty**
  - Answer public questions about an uncertain environmental risk at a meeting or by phone using the current message map
  - Draft a public advisory that states the hazard, the people affected, the uncertainty and the protective action in plain language

  - Recommend interim response and treatment options for an emerging contaminant, comparing performance evidence, cost and handling of residuals.
  - Interpret emerging-contaminant results against current and proposed criteria, stating how the conclusions change if the criteria change.
- **Develop and resolve environmental enforcement cases**
  - Investigate a reported environmental violation, establishing the facts, responsible party and applicable requirement before recommending an enforcement response
  - Assemble the evidence file for an enforcement case, linking each alleged violation to the inspection findings, records and samples that prove it
- **Communicate environmental and health risks under uncertainty**
  - Answer public questions about an uncertain environmental risk at a meeting or by phone using the current message map
  - Draft a public advisory that states the hazard, the people affected, the uncertainty and the protective action in plain language

## Natural resource and environmental programme manager — federal variant (P1)

*Function:* Keep an environmental or natural resource programme funded, lawful, staffed and able to deliver its decisions over budget and policy cycles.

*X4 match:* `skos:relatedMatch` (confidence 0.4, applies to: regulatory programmes; candidate agent draft, evidence J). *Authority position (editorial):* resource-manager.

*Credential gates (issuer verified):* 1 not shown until the issuer is verified

### Senior and lead — indicative band GS-12 to GS-13 (senior); GS-13 to GS-14 (lead); GS-14 to GS-15 (strategic) (not a classification criterion)

**Major duties (agent draft, in record order)**

*% time: set by the supervisor; EMST supplies none before job analysis.*

*Critical and needed-at-entry tasks: Assessment pending (job analysis).*

- **Formulate, justify and execute public budgets across appropriations cycles**
  - Prepare a program budget request and justification linking each funding increment to outputs and outcomes the budget office can verify
  - Reconcile program obligations and expenditures against appropriations, agreements and fee accounts each month, flagging any use outside purpose or period
  - Prepare a continuing-resolution and funding-lapse contingency plan, ranking program activities by legal requirement and consequence of delay
  - Brief appropriations staff or a governing board on a program budget request, answering questions with figures traceable to the justification
- **Assess the durability and reversal risk of policy choices and time actions to policy windows**
  - Assess the reversal risk of a program's key instruments, recording the evidence, the likely triggers and a contingency for each high-risk instrument
  - Advise leadership on the choice and timing of an instrument for a new policy, comparing the durability, speed and litigation exposure of each option
  - Classify each instrument a program relies on by type and the process needed to change it, recording who can change it and how quickly
- **Brief decision-makers and elected officials for authoritative decisions**
  - Write a decision memo for an accountable official, stating the decision required, options, evidence, risks and a recommendation within two pages
  - Brief a decision-maker orally on a pending decision under time pressure, answering questions and stating where the evidence is uncertain
  - Advise an official in writing when the evidence does not support a preferred option, recording the advice given in the decision file
  - Prepare a staff report for a governing body's public meeting, stating findings, options and the legal basis for each recommended action
- **Navigate legislative and governing-body processes for environmental programs**
  - Track bills, ordinances and appropriations measures affecting the program, summarizing each relevant provision's effect on program operations
  - Prepare testimony or a briefing for a legislative committee or governing board, stating the program's technical position and its evidence
- **Track regulatory change and translate it into operating guidance**
  - Write a dated change notice explaining what a new rule, guidance or court decision changes for staff, its effective dates and the work in progress it affects
  - Train staff on a significant regulatory change, testing their application of the new requirement on sample cases
- **Design and administer cross-jurisdictional stewardship agreements**
  - Draft a memorandum of understanding or interagency agreement that assigns shared responsibilities, resources and decision rights for a joint program
  - Monitor an agreement's deliverables, invoices and revenue ledger against its terms, amending the agreement when scope or partners change
- **Prepare and revise management plans for publicly held lands**
  - Coordinate an interdisciplinary team drafting a forest, range or refuge management plan, assigning plan components and reconciling conflicting resource objectives
  - Write plan components such as desired conditions, objectives, standards and monitoring questions so that later projects can show consistency with them
- **Administer contracts, grants and intergovernmental agreements**
  - Review a proposed agreement for compliance with procurement, grant and cross-cutting requirements before signature, listing each deficiency and its correction
- **Elicit, document and transfer tacit and institutional knowledge before people leave**
  - Identify knowledge held by one or a few people in a unit by rating its criticality and its risk of loss
  - Prepare a handover record of open commitments, contacts, site conditions and decision history for a transferred assignment
- **Design developmental work experiences that preserve the formation of professional judgment**
  - Analyze a workflow to identify which entry-level tasks form judgment and which of them AI tools or automation now perform
  - Advise leadership on the formation consequences of adopting an AI tool before deployment, naming the alternative formation route required
  - Plan rotations and mentored field assignments that give entry staff graduated exposure to the conditions their role must handle
- **Deliver environmental projects to budget, schedule and quality**
  - Review project progress against the baseline at each reporting period to decide corrective actions
- **Govern enterprise environmental data and AI portfolios**
  - Report data and AI value and risk measures for the organization's portfolio to executives, recommending investment and retirement decisions.
  - Set governance rules that keep consequential AI-assisted decisions with accountable people and that weigh affected communities' input on AI priorities.
- **Specify, evaluate and accept AI and analytics services in procurement**
  - Write technical requirements and acceptance tests for an AI or analytics service before solicitation, tied to a local evaluation set.
- **Apply safety practices and stop-work authority across field, facility and incident settings**
  - Design a unit learning-from-incidents process that links reporting channels, review triggers and pre-work briefing content
- **Apply systems thinking across ecological, institutional and technical systems**
  - Compare alternative interventions on a system map to identify leverage points and trade-offs for decision-makers
- **Evaluate and certify others' task performance against position standards**
  - Certify a candidate's qualification for a position from the completed performance record, evaluator ratings and currency evidence
- **Develop proposals and grant applications for environmental work**
  - Decide whether to pursue a funding or contract opportunity using a documented assessment of fit, capacity and competition

**Factor 1 — knowledge required (draft language; target levels are editorial drafts)**

- Knowledge of and skill in: formulate, justify and execute public budgets across appropriations cycles (EMST target senior L3, lead L4, strategic L4, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: prepare and revise management plans for publicly held lands (EMST target senior L3, lead L4, strategic L4, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: brief decision-makers and elected officials for authoritative decisions (EMST target senior L3, lead L4, strategic L4, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: design developmental work experiences that preserve the formation of professional judgment (EMST target senior L3, lead L4, strategic L4, editorial draft).
  - A by-hand quota is a set number of unaided work products a learner completes before review-and-certify credit, sized so the learner can recognize the tool's characteristic errors.
  - Practice with unguarded AI assistance can raise practice-task scores while lowering later unaided performance, so formation is assessed with at least one AI-off component.
  - A formation task is an entry-level task with high or medium tacit content through which practitioners historically built the judgment needed to check later work, including AI output.
- Knowledge of and skill in: elicit, document and transfer tacit and institutional knowledge before people leave (EMST target senior L3, lead L3, strategic L4, editorial draft).

  - Estimate at completion equals actual cost to date plus the estimated cost of remaining work; a variance is the difference between it and the approved budget.
- Knowledge of and skill in: govern enterprise environmental data and AI portfolios (EMST target lead L4, strategic L5, editorial draft).

- Knowledge of and skill in: evaluate and certify others' task performance against position standards (EMST target senior L3, lead L4, strategic L4, editorial draft).
  - An entrustment-supervision scale rates the supervision a trainee still needs, from the assessor performing the task to no supervision needed, rather than rating the trainee against peers.
- Knowledge of and skill in: apply systems thinking across ecological, institutional and technical systems (EMST target senior L3, lead L3, strategic L4, editorial draft).
  - Feedback loops and delays mean that the short-term response of an ecological or institutional system to an action can differ in sign from its long-term response.
- Knowledge of and skill in: apply safety practices and stop-work authority across field, facility and incident settings (EMST target senior L3, lead L4, strategic L4, editorial draft).
  - Stop-work authority lets any worker halt a task they judge unsafe; the task resumes only after the hazard is assessed and the plan revised, and the person who stopped it is not penalized.
  - A no-blame incident review separates system and condition causes from individual error and sanctions only reckless or wilful acts, so that people keep reporting near misses.
- Knowledge of and skill in: develop proposals and grant applications for environmental work (EMST target senior L3, lead L3, strategic L3, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: specify, evaluate and accept AI and analytics services in procurement (EMST target senior L3, lead L3, strategic L3, editorial draft).

- Knowledge of and skill in: record provenance and AI involvement in work products (EMST target senior L2, lead L2, strategic L3, editorial draft).

- Knowledge of and skill in: justify positions and staffing with workload and mission evidence (EMST target senior L3, lead L4, strategic L4, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: scan horizons and translate change signals into workforce decisions (EMST target strategic L4, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: set programme strategy and lead organizational and technological change in environmental programmes (EMST target senior L3, lead L4, strategic L4, editorial draft).

## Hazard mitigation and floodplain manager — federal variant (P2)

*Function:* Reduce disaster losses through mitigation planning, floodplain regulation and environmentally sound recovery.

*X4 match:* `skos:relatedMatch` (confidence 0.35, applies to: environmental and historic preservation review; candidate agent draft, evidence J). *Authority position (editorial):* funder.

*Credential gates (issuer verified):* Certified Floodplain Manager (CFM) (preferred)

### Developmental and full performance — indicative band GS-9 to GS-11 (journey) (not a classification criterion)

**Major duties (agent draft, in record order)**

*% time: set by the supervisor; EMST supplies none before job analysis.*

*Critical and needed-at-entry tasks: Assessment pending (job analysis).*

- **Develop hazard mitigation plans and fundable mitigation projects**
  - Conduct a hazard and risk assessment for a jurisdiction from hazard histories, exposure inventories and climate projections, documenting data limitations
  - Facilitate a mitigation planning committee to agree goals, actions and responsible agencies for a plan update
  - Prepare a benefit-cost analysis for a mitigation project following the funder's methodology, documenting every input and its source
  - Scope a mitigation project's alternatives, costs and environmental constraints to the level a funding application requires
- **Administer local floodplain management regulations and flood insurance programme requirements**
  - Review a development permit application in a mapped flood hazard area against the floodplain ordinance's elevation and construction standards
  - Make substantial-damage determinations for flood-damaged structures after an event from damage inspections and cost estimates
  - Check an elevation certificate against the permit, survey and flood map before accepting it into community records
  - Prepare the community's rating-programme documentation for floodplain activities that reduce flood insurance premiums
- **Conduct environmental and historic preservation review for disaster recovery and mitigation projects**
  - Determine the level of environmental review a disaster recovery project needs from its scope, location and available exclusions
  - Apply the floodplain and wetland decision process to a recovery project, documenting the alternatives considered and minimization measures
  - Write project conditions that carry environmental and historic preservation commitments into a recovery or mitigation funding award
- **Conduct rapid post-disaster field assessments**
  - Verify a remotely sensed damage or burn-severity map at field plots, recording where the map misclassifies conditions
  - Identify immediate post-disaster hazards such as debris-flow paths, hazard trees and spills, marking exclusion areas for responders and the public
  - Prioritize stabilization treatments for values at risk from field findings and hazard modelling, documenting the basis for each priority
- **Assess climate vulnerability of species, ecosystems, infrastructure and communities**
  - Conduct a vulnerability assessment for focal species or ecosystems with an established framework, stating the evidence and confidence for each rating.
  - Rate climate exposure, sensitivity and adaptive capacity for each management unit from documented evidence, flagging ratings that rest on expert judgment alone.
  - Synthesize vulnerability findings into ranked recommendations for managers, showing how confidence differs among the ranked items.
- **Plan climate adaptation and integrate climate risk into plans and capital decisions**
  - Facilitate an adaptation planning workshop with resource managers and stakeholders, recording the options considered and the reasons for each choice.
  - Develop climate adaptation strategies that fit the organization's mandates and planning frameworks, stating the climate assumptions each strategy depends on.
- **Communicate environmental and health risks under uncertainty**
  - Answer public questions about an uncertain environmental risk at a meeting or by phone using the current message map
  - Draft a public advisory that states the hazard, the people affected, the uncertainty and the protective action in plain language
  - Prepare a shared message map with partner agencies for an emerging environmental or health incident
- **Conduct environmental impact review of proposed actions**
  - Prepare an environmental assessment of a proposed action, analyzing the reasonably foreseeable effects of the action and its alternatives within the procedure's page and time limits *(formation task, editorial draft)*
  - Scope the review of a proposed action with cooperating agencies and the public, setting the purpose, alternatives and effects boundaries the analysis will cover *(formation task, editorial draft)*
- **Review effects of proposed actions on historic properties and resolve them through consultation**
  - Assess whether a proposed action would adversely affect each eligible property, recording the criteria and evidence applied to each finding
  - Define the area of potential effects for a proposed undertaking, documenting the direct and indirect effect pathways that justify its boundary

**Factor 1 — knowledge required (draft language; target levels are editorial drafts)**

- Knowledge of and skill in: develop hazard mitigation plans and fundable mitigation projects (EMST target journey L2, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: administer local floodplain management regulations and flood insurance programme requirements (EMST target journey L2, editorial draft).

- Knowledge of and skill in: communicate environmental and health risks under uncertainty (EMST target journey L2, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: conduct environmental impact review of proposed actions (EMST target journey L2, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: review effects of proposed actions on historic properties and resolve them through consultation (EMST target journey L2, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: interpret and question environmental data products in everyday work (EMST target journey L1, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: use AI tools responsibly in everyday environmental work (EMST target journey L1, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: validate AI-generated work products before professional use (EMST target journey L1, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: record provenance and AI involvement in work products (EMST target journey L1, editorial draft).
- Knowledge of and skill in: coordinate environmental response operations within incident command (EMST target journey L2, editorial draft).
